key_insight: Indirect prompt injection—malicious instructions embedded in untrusted inputs—requires system-level defenses (not just model-level fixes). Dynamic replanning, context-aware security constraints, and runtime instrumentation together reduce the risk that agents will execute dangerous actions.
problem_solved: Protects AI agents powered by LLMs from indirect prompt injection attacks that cause them to perform harmful or unintended actions when exposed to untrusted data in realistic, dynamic environments.
method: Advocate dynamic replanning and on-the-fly security policy updates so agents can adapt safely as tasks and contexts change.
Enforce context-dependent security boundaries (least privilege, sandboxing, and input/output constraints) to limit what untrusted instructions can affect.
Instrument agents with provenance, monitoring, and verification layers plus fail-safe policy enforcement to detect, attribute, and block suspicious influences before dangerous actions occur.
impact: Provides a practical blueprint for designing safer agent architectures; helps practitioners reduce attack surface and operational risk when deploying LLM-driven agents in the wild.
visual_elements: Flow diagram: untrusted input → agent reasoning → policy checkpoints → action/execution highlighting where injections can be blocked
Before/After schematic: agent without defenses (vulnerable) vs. agent with dynamic replanning, sandboxing, and monitoring (hardened)
Stacked architecture diagram: model layer, orchestration/replanning layer, security/policy layer, instrumentation/monitoring layer
Threat timeline: how an indirect prompt injection propagates through data → context → agent decision and where interventions occur
paper_title: Architecting Secure AI Agents: Perspectives on System-Level Defenses Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks
paper_authors: Chong Xiang, Drew Zagieboylo, Shaona Ghosh, Sanjay Kariyappa, Kai Greshake
